prompt:
Research the officially documented limits of GitHub Pages (published site size, monthly bandwidth, builds per hour). Cite GitHub's documentation page and quote the limits.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

response.content:
Based on the officially documented limits provided by GitHub, here are the specific limits for published site size, monthly bandwidth, and builds per hour:

SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/pages/getting-started-with-github-pages/github-pages-limits | QUOTE: "Published GitHub Pages sites may be no larger than 1 GB." | CLAIM: The maximum size limit for a published GitHub Pages site is 1 GB.

SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/pages/getting-started-with-github-pages/github-pages-limits | QUOTE: "GitHub Pages sites have a soft bandwidth limit of 100 GB per month." | CLAIM: The monthly bandwidth limit for GitHub Pages sites is 100 GB.

SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/pages/getting-started-with-github-pages/github-pages-limits | QUOTE: "GitHub Pages sites have a soft limit of 10 builds per hour." | CLAIM: The build limit for GitHub Pages sites is 10 builds per hour.
